<svg viewBox="0 0 640 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="width:100%;height:auto;font-family:sans-serif;">
  <rect x="50" y="30" width="120" height="40" rx="6" fill="var(--card-bg, #1e293b)" stroke="var(--primary, #3b82f6)" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="55" fill="currentColor" font-size="12" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">Client</text>
  <rect x="470" y="30" width="120" height="40" rx="6" fill="var(--card-bg, #1e293b)" stroke="var(--primary, #3b82f6)" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="530" y="55" fill="currentColor" font-size="12" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">Server</text>
  <path d="M110 80 L530 100" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
  <text x="320" y="85" fill="currentColor" font-size="11" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">1. SYN (Seq=x)</text>
  <path d="M530 115 L110 135" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
  <text x="320" y="120" fill="currentColor" font-size="11" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">2. SYN-ACK (Seq=y, Ack=x+1)</text>
  <path d="M110 150 L530 170" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
  <text x="320" y="155" fill="currentColor" font-size="11" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">3. ACK (Ack=y+1) -> ESTABLISHED</text>
</svg>
diagram_caption: TCP 3-way handshake establishing stateful sequence numbers.

content.tldr: The TCP three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) establishes reliable, stateful bidirectional transport, but is susceptible to SYN Flood exhaustion attacks.
content.simple_explanation: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) guarantees reliable delivery by synchronizing sequence numbers between hosts: 1) Client sends SYN with initial sequence number x. 2) Server reserves connection state memory in its backlog queue and responds with SYN-ACK (sequence y, acknowledging x+1). 3) Client returns ACK (acknowledging y+1), transitioning connection to ESTABLISHED. In a SYN flood attack, adversaries send thousands of spoofed SYN packets and withhold final ACKs, filling the server's half-open connection table.
content.real_world_example: A telephone reservation desk: a caller says 'Hold a table for me, I'll confirm in a moment'; if thousands of phantom callers make reservations and never confirm, legitimate diners are turned away.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: SYN flood attacks completely exhaust operating system kernel memory tables. Modern kernels defend against this using SYN Cookies: encoding connection parameters directly into the server's Initial Sequence Number (ISN) so zero server memory is allocated until the client returns a valid ACK.
